## Observations

### Rbit orchestration boundary and librqbit session alternative

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.backend-session-comparison/1`

Reviewed rbit 0.2.2 docs (https://docs.rs/rbit/0.2.2/rbit/) and the installed
registry source: rbit supplies protocol primitives, leaving piece selection,
peer coordination, bandwidth and lifecycle to the application. Current local
integration uses those real primitives; it does not assume an upstream Session.

Alternative reviewed: librqbit 9.0.1 has Session::new, add_torrent from magnet,
completion waiting, pause/unpause/delete, session limits and persistence options
in its public documentation (https://docs.rs/librqbit/9.0.1/librqbit/ and
https://docs.rs/librqbit/9.0.1/librqbit/struct.Session.html). Inference: it could
remove substantial generic session/lifecycle infrastructure. No compatibility
proof was established for this project's exact file-rank scheduler, global
payload ownership, private discovery and strict native-source gate. Its desktop
UI is a separate Tauri/web application; that UI is not an option for this contract.
The library can be considered separately from its UI, but replacing rbit conflicts
with AGENTS.md's explicit backend constraint. Retained rbit and did not add a
second backend, external torrent process or another GUI stack.

### Linux client downloads a public 6.5 GB ISO from the Internet swarm; remaining boundaries

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.complete-piece-status/16`

2026-10-26, Linux x86_64 Ubuntu 26.04.1, i7-13700H, rustc 1.99.0, master at 1ba08ab. The opt-in Internet smoke test downloaded the user-permitted Ubuntu 26.04.1 desktop ISO in 519 s, 6482409472 bytes, every piece verified twice. On the hotel's wired IPv4 link it held about 19 MB/s from 43 peers. Public torrents get:
- .torrent and magnet adds, the latter with metadata from up to four peers at once.
- Per-family HTTP(S) and UDP announces off the step loop, and a background-dialled 2048-candidate pool.
- DHT get_peers and announce_peer (real nodes accepted 6 announces in 4 minutes), plus PEX.
- MSE/PE (35 of 38 real peers encrypted).
- A fixed dual-stack listen port, an encryption setting, and opt-in NAT-PMP/UPnP IGD mapping limited to the default gateway.
- Up to 4096 files and hybrid torrents with BEP 47 pad files.
11 fuzz targets; 244 workspace tests pass.
Remaining boundaries:
- Port mapping is proven only against loopback fixtures; the hotel gateway answered neither NAT-PMP nor SSDP.
- No IPv6 Internet transfer: the IPv6 peer path is proven on ::1 only.
- No incoming peers observed, no uTP, no webseeds, no pure v2.
- The Wi-Fi stall in observation internet-download-stall is not attributed to the client.
- Pieces written after the last checkpoint are rechecked; file identity is not a content hash; the rbit fork must be re-applied on upgrade.
- Windows, and the GUI against the Internet, are untested.

### One Internet run stalled with 25 unchoking peers; not reproduced

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.internet-download-stall/3` · scope `path "crates/templartorrent-engine/**"`, `path "integration/rbit-adapter/**"`

2026-10-25, Internet run 2 of the Ubuntu ISO (perf-results/2026-10-25-internet/run2.log), IPv4 only over hotel Wi-Fi, code before the rbit get_peers fix. Verified bytes stayed at 33.7 MB from 701 s until the run was stopped at 821 s. 25 of 28 connected peers had us unchoked and the smoothed download rate decayed to 0. On 2026-10-26 the user attributed it to unstable hotel Wi-Fi; the machine is now on wired Ethernet. Run 4 completed 6.48 GB without a stall and run 5 saw none in 180 s. The harness prints lease, request, payload and peer-error state every 10 s, so a recurrence on a stable link would show which bound held. Not treated as a client defect unless it recurs on a stable connection.

**supersedes** `@templartorrent.observation.internet-download-stall/2`

### Windows socket defaults broke dual-stack listening, UDP tracker replies and the DHT loop

`verified` · `@templartorrent.observation.windows-network-defaults/2` · scope `path "integration/rbit-adapter/**"`, `path "vendor/rbit/src/dht/**"`

Running the existing loopback suite on Windows 11 showed three platform differences that would hurt real downloads there. Each is now handled. (1) IPV6_V6ONLY defaults to on, so the client's [::]:0 listener accepted no IPv4 peers; driver::bind_listener now clears it with socket2. (2) A UDP datagram larger than the receive buffer fails with WSAEMSGSIZE (10040) instead of being truncated, which failed tracker replies with more than MAX_PEERS peers; udp_announce now treats it as a full buffer. (3) An ICMP port-unreachable from an earlier send arrives as WSAECONNRESET on the next recv_from, and vendor/rbit's DHT server returned on that error, so the first offline node stopped the whole DHT. It now logs and skips ConnectionReset and 10040. Separately, the mapped-port listener task was aborted but never joined at shutdown, so its socket could outlive Driver::shutdown; it is now awaited. fs::canonicalize returns verbatim \\?\ paths on Windows; destinations now go through core::paths::canonical_dir, which strips the prefix when that is equivalent. All five fixes are in commit e244a3b, where the adapter suite passes on Windows.

**supersedes** `@templartorrent.observation.windows-network-defaults/1` · **derived_from** `@templartorrent.evidence.windows-port/1`

## Evidence

### Ubuntu 26.04.1, rustc 1.99.0, tree 2b9ca3f plus the rbit fork: 52 adapter tests passed (14 unit, 24 driver, 11 localhost, 3 multiblock). New announce unit tests: the GET keeps a passkey query and percent-encodes binary info hash and peer id, sets Host with a non-default port and Connection: close, and a bare host gets path /; https is refused with "https trackers need TLS support that this client does not build"; HTTP parsing accepts 200 with content length (ignoring trailing bytes) and chunked bodies with extensions, refuses 302, 404, truncated bodies, bad chunk sizes, a missing header terminator and a non-HTTP status line; the body parser reads compact IPv4 and IPv6 peers, dictionary peers, intervals and counts, and refuses failure reasons, missing interval, non-bencode and non-dictionary bodies. The loopback HTTP tracker fixtures in the driver, restore and multiblock tests discovered peers end to end through the new transport.

### Ubuntu 26.04.1, i7-13700H (avx2, sha_ni), rustc 1.99.0, release profile, commit bf22b04, backend detected Avx2, synthetic dense arrays, 500 iterations. eligible p50 ns scalar/auto: 1k pieces 32/36; 100k 939/929 then 697/796 on a repeat run; 1M 7968/6418 with auto p95 20803 versus scalar 9433. reference_piece_pick p50: 1k 3034 ns; 100k 171793 ns then 348377 ns on the repeat with p95 3366847 ns; 1M 4786919 ns with p95 10686525 ns. Finding: the AVX2 eligibility kernel shows no consistent advantage over scalar at any size on this CPU, and the O(P) reference piece pick dominates by two to three orders of magnitude, reaching several milliseconds per pick at 1M pieces. Run-to-run spread at 100k was about 2x on p50, so single runs are not comparable; a laptop on a live desktop session, not an isolated device.

Positive run: a 24-piece (16 KiB) two-file fixture into pre-sized zero files, checkpoint after at least 6 verified pieces (barrier set, bitmap of the verified set), transfer continued to 16 pieces, power lost: files rewritten in place to the shadow's durable image and their mtimes set back to the record's stamps; no lost piece was in the bitmap; the restart reported resume_scan note None and trusted equal to the bitmap's piece count, completed from a fresh fixture peer, and every file matched the fixture bytes.
